items.label: A
items.critique: 'valiant [Class] of [Place]! We've been expecting you!', mad urchins stealing a scepter, capitalised 'East', and the throwaway 'nettlesome urchins' reminder are classic Nox.

items.label: B
items.critique: Self-introduction by name and title, a clean threat (a hundred gold a month or the mill burns), shut gate, kill order and reward: a well-built but templated reeve speech.

items.label: C
items.critique: Stiff Latinate wizard voice ('transpiring', 'scry out', 'antiquated records') with an agreement slip ('incursions ... is') and a reminder that names items the opening masked: authentic campaign roughness.

items.label: D
items.critique: Grand travelogue exclamations ('timeless fortress home', 'glorious') and a terse 'You need to press on now, lad.' reminder fit the campaign's openings.

items.label: E
items.critique: Short clipped instructions from a companion who drops the player off ('Too many prying eyes', 'Forest beasts will heed its bite') and a gruff 'Get a move on.' reminder.

items.label: F
items.critique: Same reeve template with a proof-item twist (red cloak); the reminder and journal both restate the target and location precisely.

items.label: G
items.critique: 'Come in, stranger, and shut the door. I'm [Person], Reeve of [Place].' then threat, gate, kill, reward; competent but formula-identical to its siblings.

items.label: H
items.critique: 'I'll be plain about it' and 'nothing comes in, and nothing goes out' are writerly flourishes; the structure mirrors B, F, G and I exactly.

items.label: I
items.critique: 'I won't waste your time' plus the same name-title intro and gate-reward close; the reminder 'Is [Person] dead yet? ... Go!' is closer to Nox but still navigational.

items.label: J
items.critique: Mid-scene, terse fragments ('You'll know. And careful.') that assume context, with a longer reminder than opening; the unevenness reads authentic.

tells: New openings introduce the speaker by name and title ('I'm [Person], Reeve of [Place]'); Westwood's speakers assume the player knows them or the scene.
New openings follow a fixed three-beat arc: greeting, threat with a shut gate, kill order plus reward; Westwood's openings vary wildly in length and shape.

New reminders and journals restate target and location precisely ('Kill X in the watchtower on Y, north of Z'); Westwood's reminders are mood lines ('Go! Don't just stand there.') and journals are short.
Westwood's register is grander or stiffer (Latinate vocabulary, 'valiant', 'timeless fortress home') and carries small grammar or capitalisation slips; the new texts are uniformly clean and plain.
New texts use repeated writerly flourishes ('I'll be plain about it', 'I won't waste your time', 'nothing comes in, and nothing goes out').
